text:
maya: Heads-up — our interruption_rate for eu-central1 spiked from ~0.4% to 3.6% between 10:00–10:06 UTC. Not all instance types are affected, mostly a100-pre-emptible-ish pools. :thinking:

jordan: :eyes: link to the dashboard? is this causing any SLO alerts or pages?

maya: Grafana -> infra/gpu/spot-interruptions (panel 9). Also saw concurrent rise in provider_capacity_percent from the cloud API. I'm thinking the provider's capacity API + our eviction_score might give better fidelity than interruption_rate alone.

ops-bot: alertmanager triggered: GPU_SPOT_INTERRUPTION_HIGH (severity=page) at 1815001290 for eu-central1 (group=a100-preemptible).

liam: Can we avoid paging on 1–2 minute transients? We get noisy pages during provider-side spot rebalancing. Suggest adding a short smoothing window + composite condition before page.

maya: Agreed. Proposal: composite alert = (provider_capacity_percent < 12% sustained for 3m) AND (interruption_rate_5m > 0.02). If only one signal trips, lower to ticket (sev=notice).

sanjay: Sounds reasonable. Would also include network_flap_count > 3 in last 5m to catch infra-network-caused evictions. Otherwise we misattribute to provider.

jordan: Can you paste the PromQL you used so I can add to the panel and test?

maya: Sure — here's what I ran locally against prod metrics:
```
# interruption rate over 5m for a100 pools in eu-central1
sum(rate(spot_evictions_total{region="eu-central1", instance_type=~"a100.*"}[5m]))
/
sum(count_over_time(requests_total{region="eu-central1", instance_type=~"a100.*"}[5m]))
```
Composite alert suggestion:
```
(provider_capacity_percent{region="eu-central1", pool="a100-preempt"} < 12)
and
increase(provider_capacity_api_unavailable_total{region="eu-central1"}[3m]) == 0
and
(sum(rate(spot_evictions_total{region="eu-central1", pool="a100-preempt"}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total{region="eu-central1", pool="a100-preempt"}[5m]))) > 0.02
```

liam: Nice. For paging, wrap the composite in a for: 3m and set severity mapping with labels. Also add a secondary query for `eviction_score > 0.6` so we can triage quickly which workers to drain.

ops-bot: note: current alerting rule infra_alerts::GPU_SPOT_INTERRUPTION_HIGH has for=1m and fires pages. Will edit after dev-sig approval.

jordan: Also we should emit an internal metric `spot_signal_noise` that tracks how often provider_capacity_percent toggles >50% up/down within 10m — then we can mute alerts for noisy providers/regions automatically.

sanjay: Good call. Product-impact mapping: if the composite fires and `slo_error_budget_remaining < 5%` then escalate immediately; otherwise start with duty-notify + auto-fallback to dedicated-pool routing. We need a runbook entry for that.

maya: I'll draft the runbook steps: 1) check composite panel + recent provider API status, 2) if provider_capacity_percent <12% and eviction_score>0.6 -> trigger autoswitch to dedicated (start scale-up job), 3) if network_flap_count>3 follow network runbook, 4) file incident only if SLO impact > 0.5% in last 15m.

liam: Can you add the Grafana panel link and the query to the runbook? Also add a sample `kubectl drain` snippet we use for quick remediation.

maya: done — will push a PR to infra/runbooks/spot-signals.md and update alertmanager severity map. Planning to test in staging tomorrow 08:00 UTC.

alertmanager: Silence created for GPU_SPOT_INTERRUPTION_HIGH in eu-central1 for 2h by maya to avoid duplicate pages while we tune rules.

jordan: Thanks — please ping #oncall when the staging test is done. If the composite looks stable let's roll to prod Friday during low traffic window.

maya: Will do. Ticket: INFRA-4621 created for follow-up and dashboard changes.
